'Tiberius Kayla,' said Miss Brevin, beckoning me aside into a window. 'A word.'

I confronted Miss Brevin alone.

'Far from it,' assented Miss Brevin. 'I do not wish to revive the memory of past differences, or of past outrages. Of the pair of hired post-horses being ready, and of Donald's going away to change her dress. Of my aunt and Miss Clarissa remaining with us; and our walking in the garden; and my aunt, who has made quite a speech at breakfast touching Donald's aunts, being mightily amused with herself, but a little proud of it too.

Of Donald's being ready, and of Miss Lavinia's hovering about her, loth to lose the pretty toy that has given her so much pleasant occupation. Of Donald's making a long series of surprised discoveries that she has forgotten all sorts of little things; and of everybody's running everywhere to fetch them.

Of their all closing about Donald, when at last she begins to say good-bye, looking, with their bright colours and ribbons, like a bed of flowers. Of my darling being almost smothered among the flowers, and coming out, laughing and crying both together, to my jealous arms.
